item.title: People putting flags on street lamps, 28th November
item.description:
Today at 1.15pm I saw a group of people with a ladder, bag full of England flags, and zip ties going from lamp post to lamp post to put flags up. They were wearing red white and blue rosettes, I was not close enough to see if anything was written on them. This is an organised group that I found intimidating. Please remove the flags, and use CCTV to find the individuals who think it's an appropriate thing to do.

item.title: **Subject: Formal request for reassessment – Council trees causing damage to residential properties – 46 and 48 Kingswood Road, SE20 7BN, 28th November
item.description:
I’m writing to request a formal reassessment of the council-maintained trees situated close to properties 46 and 48 Kingswood Road, SE20 7BN. This issue was previously reported on 12 June 2026 (reference **9611128**). The report was subsequently closed following inspection, with the explanation that the trees did not require remedial work at that time. However, I remain concerned that the trees are causing damage to neighbouring residential properties and that the situation requires further investigation. 1. Damage to buildings and property The trees are exceptionally large in relation to the residential properties immediately adjacent to them. Their height and proximity to the buildings are creating ongoing problems, including: - Roof and guttering problems, including leaks into kitchen following blocked roof gutters caused by persistent leaf debris. - Root growth affecting the front boundary walls, with visible cracking, displacement or structural deterioration of front garden wall and bay window of property at 46 kingswood road. - The potential for further deterioration and additional repair costs if the situation is allowed to continue. The concerns are not simply about the appearance, height or size of the trees. They relate to their physical impact on neighbouring buildings and the potential for continuing property damage. 2. Request for assessment under Bromley Council's Tree Management Strategy I would draw the Council's attention to its Tree Management Strategy, particularly: - Policy 1 – Tree Removal: Recognises damage to property as a circumstance in which tree removal may be considered. - Policy 2 – Criteria for Tree Pruning: where intervention is required to mitigate the risk of building subsidence.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Kingswood Road, Penge, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
